Ukraine Braces for Massive Russian Strike in Next 48 Hours Ahead of Zelensky-Trump Talks — Zelensky says Russia has prepared missiles for a large-scale attack within 48 hours, as Ukrainians brace for another weekend of strikes ahead of his meeting with Trump.

She said the EU will summon Russia's envoy and propose new sanctions on its military-industrial complex.

Zelensky Warns of Massive Russian Strike Within 48 Hours — President Volodymyr Zelensky warns citizens that Russia has prepared new missiles for massive strikes that could hit Ukraine within the next 48 hours. Citing intelligence reports, he urged citizens to stay alert and called on partners to speed up air defense support.

Zelensky Tells Loomer Ukraine’s Drone Range Will Reach 10,000 Km by 2027 — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine’s drone range will grow from 3,000 to 4,000 kilometers (roughly 1,864 to 2,485 miles) this year, reaching up to 10,000 kilometers (about 6,213 miles) next year. He shared the information with US right-wing influencer and journalist, Laura Loomer, during a July meet in Kyiv.

‘You Messed Up – Fix It’: Kyiv Protesters Demand Fedorov’s Return on Day Nine — Thousands rallied in central Kyiv for a ninth straight day on Friday, welcoming President Volodymyr Zelensky’s removal of Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi but insisting their main demand remains unmet: the return of Mykhailo Fedorov as defense minister. Protesters vowed to keep up pressure until their demands are addressed.

Russian Drone Strikes Passenger Train in Dnipropetrovsk Region — A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a passenger train in the Dnipropetrovsk region. However, all passengers and crew were evacuated safely after a monitoring group detected the threat in advance.

How Ukraine’s Drone Swarms Decimated Russia’s Shadow Fleet in the Sea of Azov — In this episode of Point of Impact, former US Navy SEAL Chuck Pfarrer breaks down Operation “MoLoChKa” – a joint SBS–SBU operation that struck over 170 Russian merchant vessels, ferries, and shadow fleet oil tankers without Ukraine deploying a single large surface warship.

Russia Says It Deliberately Targeted Kyiv Region Defense Expo, Confirming Strike — Russia said it deliberately targeted a defense industry exhibition in the Kyiv region, claiming it showcased drones used in attacks on Russian territory. The ballistic missile strike killed at least 10 people and injured around 100, sparking criticism over the event’s security and organization.

Russian Agents Activate 76 Starlink Terminals in Kyiv, SBU Says — Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) detained two men in Kyiv who registered roughly 76 Starlink satellite terminals for Russian intelligence, using Ukrainian passports and a postal worker’s help. Both face life imprisonment.

Trump to Meet Zelensky in Washington Tuesday, White House Says — Zelensky is set to meet Trump in Washington on Tuesday in the latest round of high-level talks as the Trump administration presses ahead with its push to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Belarus Warns Poland of Potential Terrorist Attack — Belarus had warned Poland that a disgruntled Belarusian whose Polish residency was recently revoked is plotting a terrorist attack against an activist’s children. Despite the shaky relations between the two countries, Warsaw said it’s taking the warning seriously.

The retaliatory move came amid what some suspect to be a looming trade war between Beijing and Brussels.

10 Killed, 100 Injured After Russian Missile Hits Defense Industry Event in Kyiv Region — A Russian ballistic missile strike on a training ground in the Kyiv region hosting a defense industry event killed 10 people and injured about 100. Prosecutors have launched parallel investigations into the attack and the organization of the event, while military experts questioned why it was held within range of Russian ballistic missiles.

Georgia Hit by Nationwide Blackout — Georgia was struck by a nationwide blackout around midnight on Friday, July 24, with authorities saying the exact cause remains unknown. At the time of writing, power is partially restored to parts of the country.

Russian Airstrike on Sloviansk Kills 5, Damages Latvian Consulate — Russian forces dropped two guided aerial bombs on Sloviansk, killing five people and injuring nine. The strike damaged homes, businesses, and the Honorary Consulate of Latvia, prompting Ukrainian prosecutors to open a war crimes investigation.

Romanian F-16 Downs Unidentified Drone During Russian Strike on Ukraine — Romanian President Nicușor Dan said his country’s F-16 downed an unidentified drone violating the airspace at around 11 a.m. on Friday, adding that an investigation is ongoing to establish the full circumstances.

Kyiv Hit by Rare Daytime Ballistic Missile Strike — Kyiv Post correspondents report multiple explosions in and around the city on Friday, July 24, as the Ukrainian Air Force warns of incoming ballistic missiles in a rare daytime attack. The measure is separate from proposed secondary tariffs targeting countries that continue buying Russian energy.

Russian Bombs Destroy Nova Poshta Terminal in Izyum as 150,000 Lose Power in Chernihiv — Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with 5 missiles and 180 drones, destroying a Nova Poshta terminal in Izyum. Beginning Dec. 1, eligible widows may receive IVF or artificial insemination for five years after their spouse’s death, provided they do not remarry.

Three fires covering about 630 square meters (about 6,781 square feet) broke out.

Ukraine Hits 3 Russian Targets, Including Tanker in Black Sea, Pontoon Crossing — Ukrainian forces struck a tanker in the Black Sea, a pontoon crossing near Novoekonomichne and a Russian troop concentration in Horlivka overnight on Thursday, July 23. The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) said the operation targeted military and economic assets supporting Moscow’s war effort.

Ukraine, Raytheon Discuss Joint Patriot Interceptor Production — Ukraine is prepared to jointly produce Patriot interceptors with Raytheon as the sides seek to deepen their defense partnership, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. The proposed cooperation comes after his discussions with US President Donald Trump in Ankara, Turkey during a NATO summit.

3 Killed, 32 Wounded in Russian Attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Region — Three people were killed and 32 wounded, including a child, as Russian forces struck four districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. Nearly 40 attacks with drones, artillery, and aerial bombs damaged homes, businesses, and a fire station.

EU Sanctions Russia's Sports Minister and FIDE President in 21st Package — The EU has added Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev and International Chess Federation (FIDE) President Arkady Dvorkovich to its sanctions list under the newly agreed 21st package. The measures also freeze the oil price cap at $44.1 per barrel and target nearly 250 other individuals.

US Influencer Loomer Attacks Putin for Bombing 11th-Century Ukrainian Religious Edifice — Laura Loomer used a visit to Kyiv’s Pechersk Lavra to renounce her former pro-Russian views, saying Kremlin propaganda misled her. Ukrainian media welcomed her reversal as evidence that some influential US right-wing politicos are shifting toward support for Ukraine.

Rubio Says Russia Is Losing Over 5,000 Troops a Week in Ukraine — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Russia is losing more than 5,000 to 6,000 soldiers each week, while acknowledging that Ukraine also continues to suffer heavy military and civilian losses.

Chinese Refineries Turn to Russian, Iranian Crude Due to Choked Supplies — Private Chinese refiners are reportedly buying crude from Russia’s Far East and resumed talks with Iran for Iranian crude over supply uncertainty due to renewed fighting in the Middle East. Fedorov Turns Down Zelensky’s Offer to Become ‘Deputy PM for Military Innovations’ — The former defense minister wrote in a written response that he would accept no other position than his former post, saying it’s the only way for him to fulfill his plans to reform the military and contribute to Ukraine’s victory against Russia’s invasion.

Russia Escalating Bid to Choke Ukraine’s Grain Corridor as Ships Stay Away – Zelensky — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia is intensifying efforts to choke Ukraine’s Black Sea grain corridor after no commercial ships entered the country’s ports. The disruption has prompted major shipping companies to suspend port calls, threatening Ukraine’s exports and adding fresh pressure to global food markets.

Zelensky Confirms Ambassador Offer for Former PM Svyrydenko — Zelensky confirmed that he offered former PM Svyrydenko the post of Kyiv’s envoy to Washington alongside another unspecified alternative, but it’s unclear whether Svyrydenko took up any of Zelensky’s offer, as reports suggest that she already turned down the ambassador proposal.

$50M Buk-M3 Blown Off the Road: Ukrainian Drone Ambushes Russian Air Defense System — A Ukrainian drone struck a Russian Buk-M3 air defense system worth an estimated $50 million while it was being moved toward the front line in the Donetsk region, with Ukraine’s Border Guard calling the attack another example of low-cost drones destroying some of Russia’s most valuable military assets.

Fedorov Offered ‘Military Innovation Deputy PM’ Post, Zelensky Says — Zelensky said Thursday he offered former defense minister Fedorov the role of “deputy prime minister of Ukraine for military innovations,” but it’s unclear if the latter had accepted the offer. The proposed position would mean an entirely new ministry, which also casts doubt on whether Fedorov would have actual leverage within the system without an established ministry.

To the Ukrainians, Zelensky is Not a Hero, Just a Politician | Stefan Korshak — The dismissal of Ukraine’s popular Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has sparked protests across the country. Many saw his sacking over reported conflict with top commander Oleksandr Syrskyi as a massive blunder by President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Drones vs. Humans- Ukraine's Defense Reshuffle — Drones vs. humans is driving the evolution of warfare worldwide. It is also what is driving Zelensky's firing of both his defense minister and the general of his armies at a crucial time.

Ukrainian F-16 Shoots Down Russian Su-35 in First Aerial Kill, US General Says — The senior US general told the Senate that a Ukrainian F-16 shot down a Russian Su-35 in a recent engagement, marking the first known F-16-versus-Su-35 air combat victory. The Su-35 forms the backbone of Russia’s fighter fleet and has been exported to several countries, including Iran.

Russia's Su-57 Fifth-Generation Fighter Jet Crashes Near Moscow — A Russian Su-57 fifth-generation fighter jet crashed during a training flight near Moscow. The pilot ejected safely, no casualties were reported, and Russian authorities have not yet disclosed the cause of the incident.

Russia Warns US Against Ukraine Arms Sales as Top Diplomats Meet in Manila — Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that further American arms deliveries to Ukraine were “unacceptable” during talks in Manila, while urging a diplomatic solution. The meeting came as Kyiv seeks to revive peace efforts and Washington shifts focus back to ending the war.

Irish PM Visits Kyiv as Ireland Makes Ukraine Top EU Presidency Priority — Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin arrived in Kyiv for talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky, pledging Ireland will make support for Ukraine and its EU membership bid a top priority during its six-month presidency of the Council of the EU.

EU Agrees on 21st Russia Sanctions Package — EU ambassadors have agreed on the bloc’s 21st sanctions package against Russia after weeks of disputes over measures targeting Moscow. The deal follows objections from several member states that forced Brussels to scale back some proposals, but the package will still expand economic pressure on the Kremlin.

Russia Restricts Nighttime Shipping at its Largest Cargo Port After Ukrainian Drone Attacks — Russia has reportedly imposed nighttime restrictions at Novorossiysk, its largest cargo port, as Ukrainian attacks disrupt Black Sea shipping. The measures, alongside disruptions on Ukraine’s coast, have tightened grain export routes and pushed wheat prices higher.
